chapter: Learning music and the early bands
title: George Sr. taught Joe Oliver and the string band
summary: She insists her husband taught Joe Oliver, who played in his brass band and learned string music with his string band; Manuel Manetta also talks about him.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Well, I just laughed and talked about Joe. We were just talking about Joe. And some of them boys, you know, he taught. Did you say he taught Joe Oliver? He taught Joe. He taught Joe. And many times, he'd give somebody else a present. I'd say, well, they never say nothing about Joe, Steve and Joe. And I know that. He taught Joe and Joe played in his brass band. And when he got the string band, as they call in those days, and used to play out of the lake for all the country clubs and all the places out of the lake. Joe used to go with him and with the boys. And that's how he learned how to play the string instrument, you see. And they would all throw in and give Joe money so he could go with them. Yeah. Well, I know that myself. My children was all small. I know that.
We talked to Mrs. Oliver, Joe Oliver's wife, Mrs. Stella Oliver. Yeah. She couldn't remember the name of his teacher.

She couldn't remember. Well, George taught him. I know that much. George taught him. I don't know who else taught him. I know. I'd ask him if Mrs. Perkins and he said no. I know that. And he taught him. He taught him how to play in the string music. With the string music. And I said often he'd come. But they're always in my home. I knew them well. I knew all of them. I knew all of them. Manuel Moneta is another one.
Yes. He talks about your husband.
He talks about George all the time.
